answer: The vertex decay curve is applied at each close, opal records the drop, and voyage recomputes standing from replay. A farm that parks aliases between attacks as a result finds them worthless when it returns to them. Standing decays sharply after 4 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. Every extra alias adds 10 hours of verification and 30 percent more locked value. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
